evidence.fifthPath: src/features/streaming/MadoWorkspace.tsx handles chzzk-presentation fullscreen_toggle/fullscreen_exit and directly calls getCurrentWindow().setFullscreen. This is the fifth main-window control path, not a fifth native helper.
evidence.cause: Four native helper paths each remember only their own session.status.fullscreen and call main.set_fullscreen(false) on close/exit. Another video or provider can enter fullscreen before the old session's delayed close completes, so the old false call can take the new owner out of fullscreen. CHZZK uses the same main window without participating in any shared owner arbitration.
evidence.noExistingAuthority: Repository search found no common native main-window fullscreen owner. nativePlayerGeometry.ts has DOM-only presentation ownership; it hides native slots if more than one visible data-platform-native-fullscreen element exists, but it cannot arbitrate asynchronous native-window exits or update stale provider snapshots.
evidence.qualification: The race follows the actual asynchronous close/replace call paths and was identified by root source review. It is not claimed to have been reproduced on the desktop yet. SOOP VOD last-viewer retirement and old-alias viewport fencing are separate already implemented fixes, not a solution to cross-provider window ownership.

proposal.scope: A provider-agnostic main-window presentation coordinator only. It holds no channel/video ids, login state, media receiver, downloader, recording owner or scheduler state. Keep provider-specific availability and trusted-input checks at existing callers.
proposal.identity: Use an opaque owner id plus a monotonically increasing grant revision or random capability for each accepted acquisition. Bind each native caller's grant to its current session/document epoch. A release must present its exact grant; a stale grant is an idempotent no-op even if its session still has fullscreen=true. Main-window label/instance is part of the binding.
proposal.acquire: After the existing caller validates visibility, session and trusted input, serially request fullscreen for the main window and install the new owner/grant only if the native operation succeeds. Reacquiring the same current grant is idempotent. A new owner supersedes the old one without first turning the window out of fullscreen.
proposal.release: Exit the main window only if the provided grant is still current. Clear that owner only after successful native exit, or retain a truthful retryable state on failure. Old close, old epoch, replacement cleanup and duplicate exit must never alter a newer owner's native window state.
proposal.synchronizePresentation: Supersession must clear the previous owner's local fullscreen presentation and notify its renderer without closing or pausing media. Do not stop at guarding OS calls: leaving the previous provider's snapshot/DOM fullscreen flag true would cause two owners and hide native slots. Use weak owner-lifecycle callbacks or a generic owner-change event/revision plus exact-current snapshot reconciliation; invoke callbacks outside the coordinator lock and never import another provider's state. The implementation must specify which of these bounded approaches is chosen before editing.
proposal.serialization: Serialize the main-window mutation and owner decision so two overlapping enables/disables cannot interleave. Do not block the UI thread waiting for a callback that must run on that thread, and do not invoke provider callbacks while holding the common coordinator lock. A main-thread dispatcher or equivalent bounded non-reentrant protocol is preferable to ad-hoc asynchronous setFullscreen calls.
proposal.chzzk: Replace only the one CHZZK presentation event's direct setFullscreen call with a trusted-main-renderer presentation command/API. The component keeps a stable opaque owner id and accepted grant; toggle is based on its own current ownership, not just the OS window boolean. Retain its existing active-pane/channel filter and button event routing. No CHZZK stream, chat, recording, login or layout engine change.
proposal.lifecycle: Normal viewer close, page/session replacement, tab/provider hiding and shutdown release only the exact owned grant when the existing flow requires exiting fullscreen. Minimize and tray audio policy are unchanged; merely minimizing does not create a fullscreen release or mute. Old callback/epoch invalidation cannot transfer ownership or resurrect a closed session.
proposal.fallback: If a bounded coordinator cannot be integrated and verified safely in this batch, keep this finding explicitly open. Do not label a SOOP-only flag, isFullscreen boolean, current focus check or arbitrary DOM guess as complete cross-platform isolation.

implementationProtocol.ownership: soop_discovery_followup owns only the new platform_window_fullscreen.rs coordinator/dispatcher and pure tests; youtube_followup owns this protocol, four native helper integrations, the typed frontend API and the single CHZZK presentation handler/tests. Root owns lib registration, Cargo and actual desktop validation.
implementationProtocol.dispatch: All ownership decisions and main-window mutations serialize on the native main UI thread. Compare the main HWND thread id to GetCurrentThreadId before dispatch and execute directly when already on that thread; never queue then wait on the same thread. A reentrancy guard rejects recursive mutations without holding the owner mutex during native calls or callbacks.
implementationProtocol.queuedTimeout: A worker waits up to two seconds for a queued operation to begin. On timeout Pending-to-Cancelled compare-and-swap wins before any side effect. A later queued closure checks that state and performs no window or owner mutation. If the operation has already become Running, the caller waits for its definitive Grant/error. A running synchronous OS call has no hard deadline guarantee; returning an ordinary timeout followed by an orphan late commit is forbidden.
implementationProtocol.commitCallbacks: Acquire invokes weak on-acquired(Grant) and on-lost(Grant) callbacks in the serialized main-thread operation, outside the coordinator mutex. Native on-acquired stores the exact grant and source-local presentation flag before returning; waiting until a worker receives the result would allow a superseded grant to be installed late. On-lost clears only that exact stored grant and its original DOM/snapshot flag. Neither callback calls acquire/release recursively or changes media, authentication or recording state.
implementationProtocol.liveness: Caller validity checks Weak session lifetime, closed flag and expected document epoch before native entry and again after commit. Close marks the source closed, clones its exact grant without retaining its mutex, then releases it. If close occurs before the acquire callback installs the grant, post-commit invalidation revokes only that same grant internally; if it occurs after installation, close observes the installed grant. Source-owned callback cleanup remains idempotent.
implementationProtocol.identity: Grant serializes only an opaque owner, source document epoch, monotonic revision and main-window incarnation key. A new window incarnation invalidates old grants. Foreign or stale release is a no-op; it cannot change a newer owner's local status or the physical window.
implementationProtocol.frontend: CHZZK retains the existing active-pane/channel and trusted native event filters, serializes its presentation requests, and stores a component-local opaque owner/epoch and exact grant. Cleanup and late completion release only that grant. The revocation listener is installed before presentation actions; a bounded revoked-revision set plus exact current query rejects a grant revoked before its promise resolves. Supersession hints clear only a matching grant; no OS fullscreen boolean is treated as ownership.
implementationProtocol.failedRollback: AcquireError carries only this request's retained grant when native rollback fails. Source-local callbacks have already installed that exact capability; native helpers make one exact release retry and return the original error. Trusted-main IPC returns a typed {grant,error} outcome so the frontend retains a retryable grant without claiming success. A failed enter for a different current owner never exposes that owner's capability.
implementationProtocol.aliasAndLocks: SOOP VOD uses its current viewer alias as the opaque presentation owner and validates the newest alias again at UI dispatch. A stale alias exit captures only a matching grant. All viewer/grant/sequence locks used by the modified helper paths are dropped before dispatch waits; weak callbacks do not access the provider registry. Document replacement releases its exact grant without altering media/account/recording ownership.
